correspondence.component_scope: Chosen glaciated opening, eastward traverse, southern bend and return toward the glacier-margin lake.
correspondence.finding: The original depicts the entire opening and curved passage within the glaciated trough labeled Chickamin Glacier, south of the mapped Canada boundary. The selected route passes east across the upper ice, bends south beside the mountain mass and returns west to the northern glacier-margin lake setting. This is geographic glacier correspondence; no active stream or subglacial channel is inferred.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering, restarting within each selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Glacier-margin lake/foreland and westward upper receiving valley.
correspondence.finding: The selected continuation crosses the northwestern lake-margin/foreland setting into the lake western outlet corridor, which is mapped continuously into the westward river valley. Chickamin River is directly labeled along that receiving valley. The lake has no separately established name in this reading; the generalized path is not required to match its exact mapped shore or one active braid.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering, restarting within each selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestern mountain-valley reach and westward turn.
correspondence.finding: A continuously mapped river corridor connects the upper valley to its southwestern bend and the short westward reach. Repeated Chickamin River labels follow the selected corridor, and mapped lateral creeks join it without an intervening separate basin. The full selected parts are visible in clean original pixels.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering, restarting within each selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Southbound enclosed valley and broad lower junction floor.
correspondence.finding: The selected river continues south through the mountain corridor and opens into a wider braided/wetland receiving floor. South Fork Chickamin River approaches from the east and joins this same floor. The selected route is the mapped Chickamin main corridor; the South Fork is a separate adjoining branch and is not an alias for the whole selection.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering, restarting within each selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestward lower-valley bend to the mainstem fragment boundary.
correspondence.finding: The original shows a continuous broad channel-and-wetland floor carrying the selected northwestward bend toward the separately labeled Leduc River approach from the north. Chickamin River labels continue through this receiving setting. The FID9122 ending and FID9123 opening occupy the same downstream valley; stored fragment and part boundaries are retained without joining or geometry editing.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering, restarting within each selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Downstream westward bend, southwestward valley and coastal approach.
correspondence.finding: The selected downstream fragment follows the mapped Chickamin River valley west and then southwest through broad meanders. Lateral creek joins and the lower branching channel belt are visible all the way to the estuarine approach. No lake-to-river transfer or separate-basin link is left unestablished.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering, restarting within each selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Chickamin mouth and separately retained rendered coastal extension.
correspondence.finding: The stored source endpoint lies in the mapped lower Chickamin estuarine channel/mouth setting. The stored rendered endpoint is farther southwest at the adjoining southeastern coastal margin of the receiving marine inlet; on this map it is not asserted to occupy the same river thread or an exact waterline. The final generalized extension traverses that coastal-margin setting. Both positions were compared separately with original pixels, and the supplied sea-terminal classification is retained as metadata. The map establishes one coastal receiving setting, without claiming a natural river course along the entire extension or assigning an unobserved marine-waterbody name.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering, restarting within each selected fragment.

findings.assignment_region_correction: The inventory region hint and initial border-area orientation are not country evidence. The inspected original places the selected path on the Alaska side of the international boundary.

correspondence.component_scope: chosen southeastern opening
correspondence.finding: The selected first southern side-valley approaches the clearly visible east–west receiver near the first/second-part transition. The receiver and a separate northern junction are readable, but haze, cloud and canopy obscure the intervening trough and southern side-valley mouth. The ordinary valley connection itself cannot be distinguished confidently from forested slope texture. This is not merely an unseen wet thread, exact bank or first coordinate. Regional prose does not locate this short chosen branch.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering, restarting within each selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: upper westward receiving valley
correspondence.finding: The narrow receiving channel is visible beneath forested valley walls, turns west and receives a separate northern tributary before continuing through the same valley. The photograph supports ordinary valley and junction correspondence throughout these parts, while the opening upstream is kept separate. No exact named boundary is read from imagery.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering, restarting within each selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: northwestward foothill corridor and major join
correspondence.finding: The selected route follows a continuous valley northwest out of steeper terrain into the forested lowland, then reaches a major northern-branch junction at the head of the prominent southward loop. Imagery establishes the approach and junction. The positional interpretation of this receiving junction as the Barco-area join is supported by the two original prose accounts and their distinctive downstream directional sequence.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering, restarting within each selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: large southwest then north loop
correspondence.finding: The same visible lowland river makes the selected large southwestward excursion, rounds its southern end and returns north. There is no separate-basin jump or missing lake transfer. The municipal account describes the corresponding Cajambre course from Barco southwest to El Llano and then north toward Aragón.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering, restarting within each selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: northwestward middle and lower meanders
correspondence.finding: The route continues northwest along a widening, repeatedly bending lowland river. Visible tributary mouths and bends connect the northern end of the loop to the lower estuarine reach. Sparse clouds do not obscure the ordinary receiving corridor or introduce another material gap. No lake, glacier or managed impoundment passage is implicated.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering, restarting within each selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: lower tidal channel to mouth
correspondence.finding: The stage-2 selection follows the same lower channel, first north and then west through a broad estuarine bend to the coastal aperture. Forested/mangrove-like islands and adjoining tidal branches are visible. The lower branch does not require a cross-land or lake-to-feeder transfer. Source prose identifies the corresponding receiving mouth as Boca Cajambre.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering, restarting within each selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: actual source and render endings
correspondence.finding: The stored source endpoint is in the broad mouth-channel setting. The render endpoint is displaced mainly south, slightly west, into the same broad estuarine receiving water. Both are short of a claim to the exact outer ocean shoreline; the visible estuarine aperture continues west to Pacific coastal water. Their different positions are preserved, not repaired or equated.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored-part numbering, restarting within each selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen eastern gully and northward receiving creek
correspondence.finding: The chosen eastern opening occupies a small mapped unnamed feeder valley. It joins the northward Bull Creek corridor, which reaches the Deep Creek receiving channel. Skedaddle Creek farther south is a separate drainage and is not substituted for this opening.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices within the sole selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Deep Creek, northwestward fan and highway-side receiving floor
correspondence.finding: The selection follows the directly labeled Deep Creek northwestward through the low mountain-front corridor and onto the open floor east of Secret Creek. The westward continuation crosses the highway-side alluvial floor into the mapped Secret Creek drainage. Channel linework is discontinuous across the final open interval, but the mapped low receiving floor is continuous without a separate enclosed lake or intervening divide. This is ordinary geographic correspondence, not a claim of a continuous wet channel or current managed operation.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices within the sole selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestern Secret Creek corridor and north/west Shaffer Mountain passage
correspondence.finding: The selected middle parts follow Secret Creek southwest across the plain, enter the mapped gorge along the north and west sides of Shaffer Mountain, and emerge at the lower Willow Creek corridor. Mud Flat and Little Mud Flat lie separately east of this passage. The direct map establishes the selected gorge route; the Basin Plan table lists a different regional Snowstorm/Petes hierarchy and is not used to rename this reach.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices within the sole selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Willow Creek and Susan River join
correspondence.finding: The lower map directly shows Willow Creek approaching and joining the eastward Susan River north of Standish and west of Litchfield. Wards Lake is an adjacent feature, not a required lake transit. Generalized selected positions remain within the connected receiving corridor; no exact bank fitting is asserted.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices within the sole selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Susan River, slough/wetland and agricultural receiving plain
correspondence.finding: The long final stored part first occupies the lower Susan receiving corridor, then turns southeast across its continuous slough/wetland and agricultural floor toward Dill Slough and the Whitehead Slough corridor. Mapped side channels, canals, fields and wetland passages are components of this common receiving plain. The whole part is not assigned to a single precise managed channel; no current diversion operation is inferred. Nearby Hartson Slough and Hartson Lake remain distinct from the final selected approach.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices within the sole selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestern lake entry and selected interior ending
correspondence.finding: The final continuation passes from the Whitehead Slough-side receiving margin into the large terminal lake basin and ends within its interior, east of the separately mapped Hartson Lake management area. The official geographic table identifies Honey Lake as the internally drained saline receiver of the Susan River. A named natural river is not projected across the lake interior.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices within the sole selected fragment.

terminal_distinctions.source_endpoint_description: Stored source ending lies within the Honey Lake interior beyond the selected northwestern slough-margin entry.
terminal_distinctions.render_endpoint_description: Stored render ending is coincident with the source ending in the Honey Lake interior; it is not a separate outlet or a named river mouth.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southwestern wetland feeder and first unnamed lake sequence
correspondence.finding: Original maps show the chosen wetland/small-stream setting, an initial rounded lake and several elongated lakes north and east. Local channels and individual lake settings are visible, but the complete selected west-then-north and eastward lake-to-lake sequence is not established throughout. The eastern continuation of part 1 is not accepted merely because nearby lakes and wetlands occupy one low plain.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices within the sole selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeastern wetland and small-lake passage crossing the Niklavik neighborhood
correspondence.finding: The selection turns northeast and crosses the mapped Niklavik Creek neighborhood before turning north toward Tractor Lake. The maps show multiple branching minor streams and separate lakes; they do not establish the entire selected transfer from this west/east drainage into the northward lake approach. Niklavik is a bounded mapped name, not proof of the modeled through-route.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices within the sole selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Tractor Lake and successive northern neighboring lakes
correspondence.finding: The selection passes through Tractor Lake and then turns east/northeast across narrow intervening land and additional lake settings into the southern part of a larger northern lake, followed by an eastward exit. The needed transfer from the selected eastern Tractor Lake margin to the next narrow lake, onward northern interlake links, and the selected eastern exit are not all demonstrated by the inspected cartography. These are specific lake-to-lake/source-feeder gaps, not a demand for exact bank matching or current wetness. The northern lake label was too small for a confident spelling and is not promoted to a name observation.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices within the sole selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastern wetland descent toward the Inaru meander corridor
correspondence.finding: A minor-stream network and the downstream approach to Inaru are mapped, but the entire selected connection from the northern lake-chain exit to that feeder is not established. The mapped lower approach does not close the missing upstream lake transfer.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices within the sole selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Connected lower river and meander corridor
correspondence.finding: These parts correspond at ordinary scale to the directly labeled Inaru River meanders and downstream widening. Generalized positions sometimes cut across meander interiors, but the same uninterrupted receiving river corridor is clear. Northern lake outlets and the major Meade River system to the south remain distinct.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices within the sole selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Inaru entry, lake passage and southern-lobe render ending
correspondence.finding: The selected rendered continuation follows the lower Inaru approach into the western/southwestern Sisgravik Lake setting and ends within its southern lobe. Map network labels extend across lake water; that does not make the lake a river alias. The source endpoint is stored separately and lies near the adjacent Kuyanak Bay-side northern margin; no exact shoreline or narrow-neck hydraulic connection is inferred from the generalized metadata.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored-part indices within the sole selected fragment.

terminal_distinctions.source_endpoint_description: Stored source ending lies near the northern margin of Kuyanak Bay, immediately south of the southern Sisgravik Lake lobe; exact bank placement is not established.
terminal_distinctions.render_endpoint_description: Stored render ending is displaced northeast from the source ending and lies within the mapped southern lobe of Sisgravik Lake after the selected lower Inaru approach.
terminal_distinctions.terminal_metadata_limit: The stored sea class is preserved as inventory metadata; it is not used to override the inspected lake/bay distinction or assert a new observed coast line.
